summary: I read the whole days-61-70 export (2,669 lines): every Arabic string with its harakat, case endings, agreement, numerals and verb forms; every translation and literal; every seg, tap gloss, quiz answer key, mistake card and grammar note; and the ⟶ transliterations. I checked 487 Arabic-bearing strings (with ⟶ lines) and 211 seg lines; 10 Arabic strings are wrong, all minor (3 × الْيَوْم without its fatha at the start of a clause, still there from round 2; 7 × إِنْجْلِيزِيَّة with a double sukūn, against إِنْجِلِيزِيَّة elsewhere in the course). Tap glosses: 696 checked (278 distinct word=gloss pairs on 276 tap lines); 13 wrong or misleading (4 أَغْلَى and 4 الْخَزْنَة with a duplicated sense, 4 مُسَافِر = 'traveller' where the lesson and quiz teach 'travelling', 1 أُسْتَاذَة = 'teacher (f)' in a note about non-teachers). Round-2 fixes are in place: أَكْبَرُ and مِنْ now show the superlative/'than' senses, الْوَاحِدَة = one, اسْمُهَا without kasra, اِسْتَعْمَلَ as a past form, l-ʿayn lower case. The Arabic itself is clean: comparatives and superlatives (أَكْبَرُ مَدِينَة, مِنْ أَكْبَرِ الْمَسَارِح, accusative apposition أَشْهَرَ مَكَان), numbers and their counted nouns (عِشْرِينَ مِلْيُونَ, أَرْبَعَةِ مَلَايِين, سِتَّةِ آلَافِ, عَشْرِ دَقَائِق, ثَمَانِمِئَةِ دَرَجَة), duals, subjunctives after أَنْ, kāna/laysa predicates, imperatives and hamza seats are correct, and all 70 quiz answer keys are right with no second correct option. 9 errors, 0 major and 9 minor: 4 gloss, 2 arabic, 3 engine (empty brackets for bare letters in all seven pronunciation prompts; the clitic hyphen rule not applied to ~17 inflected forms; Karīm, Shīkāghū and Wādī never capitalised). Pattern: the remaining problems are in the glossary layer (single-sense or duplicated entries) and the transliteration engine, not in the lesson Arabic.
